findings.failure_scenario: Run the command on source-slack: the manifest's templated JsonFileSchemaLoader is stripped by _remove_reference and the 4 manifest streams are inlined, so the substring check passes and shutil.rmtree deletes the whole schemas dir — including threads.json, which the Python-defined Threads stream (source.py get_threads_stream / streams.py Threads) still loads at runtime, breaking its schema discovery. Same for source-zendesk-support, where schemas/tickets.json is a stub `{"$ref": "tickets.json"}` delegating to schemas/shared/tickets.json (the real 4.5KB schema) — the shared file is deleted. All steps return SUCCESS, so RestoreInlineState._cleanup runs instead of the restore and the deletion is permanent in the working tree.
findings.summary: RemoveUnusedJsonSchamas deletes the entire schemas directory whenever the rewritten manifest no longer contains the substring "JsonFileSchemaLoader", ignoring schema files that are still consumed outside the manifest.

findings.failure_scenario: Run the command on source-sentry (streams list is `- $ref: "#/definitions/events"` etc.): _remove_reference deletes definitions.schema_loader (templated JsonFileSchemaLoader) and the `$ref` schema_loaders in base_stream_full_refresh/base_stream_incremental, then every stream entry is a dict whose only key is "$ref", _get_stream_name returns None, and all streams are skipped. The rewritten manifest has no schema_loader anywhere; combined with the cleanup step this deletes all of schemas/*.json (events.json, issues.json, project_detail.json, projects.json, releases.json) with no inline replacement. source-freshdesk and source-zendesk-support use the same dict-form entries and hit the same total schema loss.
findings.summary: The stream loop only resolves string-form stream entries; dict-form `$ref` entries like `- $ref: "#/definitions/events"` fall through to _get_stream_name, get no name, and are silently skipped, so no inline schema is written for them while _remove_reference has already stripped their schema_loader config from the manifest.

findings.failure_scenario: Run the command on source-mixpanel: the engage stream's schema_loader is `type: CustomSchemaLoader, class_name: source_mixpanel.components.EngageJsonFileSchemaLoader`, whose get_json_schema() dynamically fetches additional properties from the Mixpanel API and merges them into the schema (see components.py lines 304-340). The loop replaces it with `{type: InlineSchemaLoader, schema: <static engage.json>}`, so the engage stream silently loses its dynamically discovered schema properties. For any stream whose name has no matching top-level json file, the replacement is left as `schema_loader: {}` — an empty loader written into the manifest where a working loader used to be.
findings.summary: Every stream whose schema_loader is not an InlineSchemaLoader has it unconditionally overwritten, so CustomSchemaLoader (and any future non-inline loader) is destroyed and replaced by a static inline schema or an empty `schema_loader: {}`.

findings.failure_scenario: Run the command over many connectors (no --name filter): any selected connector with a .json file in its schemas dir that is not valid JSON (or empty) raises JSONDecodeError inside InlineSchemas._run; run_steps propagates it, run_connector_steps restores that one connector and re-raises, and run_connectors_pipelines' task group has no per-connector exception handling, so the whole command crashes and no reports are produced for any connector.
findings.summary: json.load on every top-level json file in the schemas dir raises on malformed content, and run_connector_steps re-raises after restore, so a single invalid schema file aborts the entire multi-connector batch with an unhandled traceback.

findings.failure_scenario: A connector whose two streams share one schema file (e.g. two streams whose JsonFileSchemaLoader file_path resolves to the same foo.json): the first conversion inlines foo.json and unlinks it, the second consumer logs "Stream foo not found in JSON schemas" and keeps its JsonFileSchemaLoader; the stream loop then replaces that loader with `schema_loader: {}` (line 196) because it is not InlineSchemaLoader, and the cleanup step deletes the rest of the schemas dir — the second stream ends up with no schema and the file is gone.
findings.summary: _update_inline_schema unlinks the json file and pops it from the shared dict after the first consumer, so a second stream or loader referencing the same schema file is left dangling and then overwritten with an empty schema_loader.

findings.failure_scenario: When a templated JsonFileSchemaLoader reference is removed, the intended log line (evidenced by the f-string matching the logger.info style of the surrounding lines) is silently discarded, so migration logs contain no trace of which references were removed — a maintainability defect in the new tool's diagnostics.
findings.summary: Dead code: `(f"    Removing reference: {loader.ref}")` is a bare parenthesized string expression with the logger.info call missing, so the removal message is never emitted.

findings.failure_scenario: run_connector_steps catches an exception or a FAILURE result and calls restore_original_state.run() instead of _cleanup(), so the temp directory made in __init__ (tempfile.mkdtemp + copytree of all schemas) is never removed; every failed migration run leaves the backup tree on disk.
findings.summary: The mkdtemp backup directory created in RestoreInlineState.__init__ is only deleted by _cleanup, which is skipped on the failure/exception path, leaking one temp directory (with a full copy of the schemas) per failed run.

findings.failure_scenario: Running the command on a connector with any unconsumed schema file (e.g. source-slack's threads.json) prints "!! JSON schema not found: threads" even though the file exists on disk, misdirecting anyone investigating why a schema was not inlined (the real reason is the stream-loop skip or a name mismatch, not a missing file).
findings.summary: After writing the manifest, the step logs "!! JSON schema not found: {name}" for every remaining entry in json_streams, but those files do exist — they were simply not consumed by any stream.

findings.failure_scenario: For any manifest-only connector (manifest.yaml at the code root, e.g. source-cin7), python_source_dir_path resolves to code_directory/source_<name>, which does not exist, so schemas_dir.is_dir() is always False and the step returns SKIPPED with "The connector does not have a schemas directory" — the declared support for MANIFEST_ONLY candidates can never trigger, contradicting the step's documented candidate conditions.
findings.summary: CheckIsInlineCandidate lists ConnectorLanguage.MANIFEST_ONLY as a candidate, but the schemas-dir check uses python_source_dir_path / "schemas", a path that does not exist for manifest-only connectors, so the MANIFEST_ONLY branch is dead and manifest-only connectors are always skipped.
